title: Community Guidelines • PARA
description: Community guidelines for PARA—rules for safe, respectful, and authentic participation on PARA services built on open civic and AT Protocol–style infrastructure.
content: Support / Community guidelines Support Community guidelines Last updated: PARA is a civic social application and related experience operated for public participation in political life. It is built on open, AT Protocol–style infrastructure that can interoperate with other services. Together with the PARA Terms of Service , Privacy Policy , and the copyright section of our terms, these Community Guidelines (“Guidelines”) govern your use of PARA applications, websites, and services we operate (collectively, “PARA”). By accessing or using PARA, you agree to these Guidelines. Please read them carefully. These Guidelines apply to social and civic networking that happens on PARA services we host. If you use another application on the same open network that is not operated by us (a “Third-Party Application”), that application’s own terms govern your experience there. We are not responsible for Third-Party Applications’ content, moderation, or practices. Our mission is to make political identity, policy expression, and civic participation easier to navigate without collapsing into generic feeds or partisan packaging. We want a community that takes disagreement seriously, protects vulnerable participants, and can evolve as law and norms change. These Guidelines are part of your agreement with us and set baseline rules for using PARA. We intend these Guidelines to comply with applicable law and to: Empower user choice: Where the product allows, we want you to control labels, safety settings, and how you present political context—consistent with legitimate safety and legal obligations. Cultivate a civic environment: We aim for spaces where people can disagree, clarify positions, and participate without harassment, hate, or coordinated harm. Evolve with feedback: We will review and update these Guidelines as PARA matures, as risks change, and as regulators clarify expectations. Unless otherwise defined here, capitalized terms follow the PARA Terms of Service. Words such as “including,” “includes,” “such as,” and “for example” mean “without limitation.” How we moderate These Guidelines exist so participation stays legible, accountable, and safe enough for public civic life. We may use human review, automated signals, and user reports. We also design for composable safety tools—such as labelers and user controls—where the protocol and product support them, so communities can add context on top of baseline rules we enforce. We respect human rights and freedom of expression, and we follow applicable law in the jurisdictions where we operate. We try to use proportionate actions—warnings, limits, removal, or account suspension—based on severity, intent, and risk. We can get decisions wrong; when we offer an appeals path for a given surface, use it to explain why you believe we erred. Even with appeals, we retain discretion to make final calls about specific content or accounts on services we operate. For how identity, moderation, verification, and privacy features are meant to work in the product, see Trust and safety and the documentation. Our principles Safety first: No content that shows, promotes, or coordinates violence, exploitation, serious self-harm, or criminal harm to people or animals; protect privacy and minors. Respect others: No harassment, hate, or discrimination targeting people based on protected characteristics or civic participation. Be authentic: No scams, impersonation meant to mislead, coordinated inauthentic manipulation, or undisclosed paid persuasion presented as organic speech. Follow the rules: Obey applicable law, respect intellectual property, do not attack our systems, and do not evade enforcement. 1. Safety first Public safety Do not use PARA to coordinate, recruit for, or promote: Criminal enterprises, terrorism, human trafficking, or violent extremist activity. Step-by-step instructions intended to enable serious crimes or terrorist acts, or coordination of harmful real-world acts (including swatting or mob violence). Do not share graphic violence to glorify harm, terrorize victims, or support criminal operations. Context matters: discussion of violence in news, art, fiction, games, or regulated sport is not banned solely because violence appears—what we restrict is real-world harm, glorification, or coordination of abuse. Child safety We apply strict rules to content and conduct involving minors: No sexualization or exploitation of minors or minor-aged characters (including synthetic, illustrated, or animated depictions when used for sexual gratification or grooming). No grooming, solicitation of intimate imagery from minors, or attempts to meet minors for abuse. No sharing identifying information, real-time location, or other sensitive details about minors that create safety risk. No unlawful advertising or promotion of gambling, controlled substances, alcohol, tobacco, or deceptive fi

title: Support • PARA
description: Contact PARA for help, read policies and legal information, and find channels for regulatory and law-enforcement requests.
content: Support PARA Support If you need help, email us at with a description of your issue and information about how we can help you. Policies and legal Documents that govern participation Legal requests Regulatory, official, and other legal contact Use the channel that matches your role. We handle requests in English unless we agree otherwise in writing. Include enough detail for us to locate the relevant material without speculative fishing expeditions. Global Regulatory Compliance Reporting Process For members of the public reporting content under local law or specific regulatory frameworks, email with jurisdiction, statutory basis, links or identifiers, and the remedy you seek. Official Requests Portal Law enforcement, government agencies, regulators, and designated competent authorities should use . Include authority, contact verification, narrow scope, and legal process where applicable. We do not operate a separate self-serve portal yet; describe what you need in the first message. EU Digital Services Act contact PARA's contact point under Regulation (EU) 2021/784 is . Requests must be made in English. Everything else legal If your request does not fall within the above three categories, email us at with a clear subject line and enough context to route the message. Also useful Read the thesis The democratic problem, the second-layer idea, and why PARA exists. Trust and safety How identity, moderation, verification, and account control work in the product.

title: Copyright Policy • PARA
description: Copyright policy for PARA—how to report infringement and how we handle takedown requests.
content: Support / Copyright policy Legal Copyright policy How we handle copyright concerns about content shared through PARA services. Reporting infringement If you believe material on PARA infringes your copyright, email with the following information: Identification of the copyrighted work you claim has been infringed. Identification of the material you claim is infringing, including enough detail for us to locate it (for example, a link or post identifier). A good-faith statement that the use is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law. Your contact details. A statement under penalty of perjury (where required by law) that your notice is accurate and that you are the copyright owner or authorized to act on the owner’s behalf. We may remove or restrict material consistent with law and policy. We will notify the user who posted the material when we act, unless prohibited by law. Counter-notice If your material was removed and you believe it was a mistake or misidentification, you may submit a counter-notice to with: Identification of the material that was removed and where it appeared. A good-faith statement that you believe the material was removed as a result of mistake or misidentification. Your contact details and consent to jurisdiction. Repeat infringers We may suspend or terminate accounts of repeat infringers where appropriate. Related Terms of service Full terms including IP provisions. Support Help and legal routing.

title: Find Friends Privacy Policy • PARA
content: Support / Find friends privacy Legal Find Friends Privacy Policy Last updated: What this covers This policy describes how PARA handles address-book and contact-matching data when you choose to use find-friends features. It supplements the main Privacy Policy . What we collect If you opt in to contact matching, we may process hashed or encrypted representations of contacts from your device address book solely to suggest connections. We do not store raw contact details longer than necessary to perform the match. How we use it Contact data is used only to generate suggestions. We do not sell contact information, use it for advertising, or share it with third parties outside the matching operation. Your control You can revoke contact-matching permission at any time through product settings. Revocation stops future matching and triggers deletion of stored match data where technically feasible. Contact Questions: . Related Privacy policy Main privacy statement. Support Help and legal routing.

title: Patent Non-Aggression Pledge • PARA
content: Support / Patent pledge Legal Patent Non-Aggression Pledge Last updated: Our commitment PARA pledges not to initiate patent litigation against anyone for using, modifying, or distributing PARA open-source software, protocol implementations, or documentation, so long as they do not first assert patents against PARA or its users. Scope This pledge covers: Use of PARA software and services for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial. Modification and distribution of PARA open-source code under its published licenses. Development of compatible applications, clients, or tools that interoperate with PARA infrastructure. Limitations This pledge does not extend to parties who first assert patent claims against PARA, its contributors, or its users. It also does not waive trademarks, copyrights, or other IP rights. The pledge is not a license and does not create any contractual obligation beyond the stated commitment. Contact Questions: . Related Terms of service Full terms including IP provisions. Support Help and legal routing.

title: Privacy Policy • PARA
description: Privacy policy for PARA websites, apps, and related services operated by the project.
content: Support / Privacy policy Legal Privacy policy High-level statement for the public site and PARA services we operate. Federation and third-party hosts introduce additional processors; your counsel should review end-to-end flows before launch. What we may collect Depending on the surface, we may process account identifiers, content you submit, technical logs needed to run the service, and communications you send to support or legal addresses. We aim to collect the minimum needed for civic features, safety, and reliability. How we use information We use data to operate and improve the product, enforce policies, comply with law, and protect users. Automated decisions, if any, are described in product documentation rather than hidden here; refer to the docs for feature-specific behavior. Protocol and federation PARA is designed around open, AT Protocol–style civic infrastructure. Federating or bridging data to other services may mean additional copies of public material exist outside our direct control. Use the schema and architecture docs to understand what is replicated where. Retention and deletion We retain information as long as needed to operate the service and meet legal obligations. You can request deletion or export help through ; we will respond when staffing allows and when your request is verifiable. Contact Questions about this policy: . Related Terms of service Rules for using hosted PARA services. Trust and safety Safety model and user-facing controls. Support Help and legal routing.

content: Support / Protocol privacy Legal PARA AT Protocol Network Services Privacy Policy Last updated: What this covers This policy describes how PARA handles data for protocol-level infrastructure services—such as relays, identity resolution, and repository sync—that support the open network. It supplements the main Privacy Policy . Public data AT Protocol–style infrastructure is designed around public repositories. Most content you post through PARA is public by default and may be replicated by other services on the network. We do not control how third-party applications index, display, or retain public data. Technical logs We retain minimal technical logs needed to operate infrastructure—such as request metadata, error rates, and abuse signals. These logs are not used for advertising profiling. Federation When data is federated to other services, those services operate under their own privacy policies. We encourage you to review the policies of any third-party application you use. title: Terms of Service Amendment for Government Users • PARA
pageTitle: Terms of Service Amendment for Government Users • PARA
description: Additional terms that apply when government entities use PARA in an official capacity.
content: Support / Government amendment Legal Terms of Service Amendment for Government Users Last updated: Scope This amendment applies when a government entity, agency, or instrumentality uses PARA in an official capacity. It supplements the PARA Terms of Service and Community Guidelines . Where there is a conflict between this amendment and the general Terms, this amendment governs for government use. Account setup and verification Government accounts must be clearly labeled as official and must use contact information tied to the entity’s domain or other verifiable channel. We may request additional documentation to confirm status before granting official designations. Content and conduct Government users are expected to follow the same Community Guidelines as all other users. Additionally, government accounts may not use PARA to: Spread disinformation or manipulate civic discourse through covert influence operations. Target individuals for surveillance or harassment outside lawful process. Suppress lawful speech or misuse reporting systems to remove content that is merely critical of the government. Data access and legal process Government requests for user data must follow the legal request channels described on our Support page. We do not provide bulk or warrantless access to user content. Emergency disclosures are limited to imminent threats of serious harm. Contact Government entities with questions about this amendment should contact before creating official accounts or initiating bulk use. Related Terms of service General terms for all users. Support Help and legal routing.

title: About • PARA
content: About PARA A second political layer for a more plural democracy. PARA started from a dream of democratic renewal in Mexico: a political social network where anonymity, public reasoning, policy disagreement, and evolving agents can work together instead of competing. The thesis is simple. Democracy stays thin when most opinions never become legible, comparable, or materially consequential. PARA is meant to reduce that friction and turn political participation into something more structured than vibes, slogans, and party packages. Origin Mexico-first thesis shaped by plural political identity, not only coalition logic. Surface Communities, matters, policy posts, representatives, trust flows, and messaging. Method Protected speech, structured disagreement, civic data, and assisted reasoning. Stack AT Protocol foundations underneath, with PARA-specific civic intelligence on top. PARA is not trying to simulate politics. It is trying to make political identity, policy conflict, and civic participation easier to express and compare. Diagnosis The problem is not opinion. The problem is friction. Most people can tell you what feels wrong. Very few can turn those views into something clear, visible, and politically consequential. PARA starts from that gap. Why ordinary politics feels thin Too much work to express a policy position clearly. Too little visibility for independent or minority political views. Too much pressure to buy an entire partisan package at once. Too little infrastructure for comparing opinion, doctrine, and action. What PARA is trying to reduce The product is meant to lower the cost of political expression, preserve disagreement, and make positions easier to compare across users, communities, parties, and representatives. Political Identity Political identity should exist before party loyalty. PARA takes inspiration from political-compass memes and from Democracy 4 because both make ideology and tradeoffs more legible to ordinary users. The goal is not to trap people inside a meme. The goal is to turn that accessibility into a more serious identity layer. Communities Beliefs can organize before party branding does. Users should be able to find a political home around ideas, nonants, or issue clusters, without collapsing immediately into the same polarized coalition script. Comparison Disagreement can become usable data. The app is designed to turn intergroup disagreement into something visible and comparable instead of leaving it as pure noise, outrage, or timeline heat. Second Layer PARA does not need to replace every network to become useful. The second-layer thesis is practical. Users can keep their reach elsewhere while PARA becomes the hub for political context, validation, search, and structured comparison. Identity links Users can connect identities and discourse across networks. Political context PARA hashtags can carry meaning even when posts travel outward. Civic hub Search, validation, and analysis can live here even when conversations begin elsewhere. Policies, Matters, RAQ Opinion becomes more useful when it can be structured. PARA introduces dedicated political flairs and voting surfaces so people can express both direction and intensity instead of posting only generic sentiment. Political flairs #POLICY|| and #MATTER| #POLICY|| anchors policy proposals and preferences. #MATTER| anchors agendas, controversies, and collective attention. Together they create dedicated civic surfaces instead of generic posting slots. Voting model Direction plus intensity Users can vote from -3 to +3 , then layer quadratic voting on top. The goal is to capture how strongly people agree or disagree, not only whether they clicked yes. The RAQ test, or Rightfully Asked Questions , belongs to the same thesis: question yourself, quantify what you believe, and turn disagreement into a more legible political dataset. Agents and civic intelligence Communities can produce shared datasets through votes, posts, and explicit disagreement. Personal and collective agents can support education, entertainment, and assisted writing. Embeddings, clustering, classification, and anomaly detection can improve search and comparison. Anonymity and validation Anonymity matters for freedom of thought and protected participation. Validation matters for trust, governance, representation, and reputation. The platform is meant to hold both at once instead of forcing every user into public exposure. Product surfaces Six ideas that do most of the explanatory work. PARA is built around concrete civic surfaces that reduce friction between thought, expression, and political consequence. Reduces Culture A political network still has to feel alive. PARA was ideated as a tool for progress: denouncing injustices, finding a political community, debating in public, proposing policy, rotating collective attention across issues, and still leaving room for humor, memes, and messy conflict. title: Trust and Safety • PARA
content: Trust and safety Protected speech needs real safety infrastructure. PARA depends on a difficult balance: anonymity where thought needs protection, validation where civic participation needs legitimacy, and enough moderation and account control that public politics does not collapse into chaos. This page sits outside the docs shell on purpose. Trust and safety is not just another subsection of reference material. It is a first-order product surface that shapes how identity, participation, and governance can work at all. {#each [ , , , ] as pillar (pillar.title)} Design principle If the product does not make exit legible, the consent is not real. Account deletion, data export, and appeals are not afterthoughts. They are part of the trust surface. Every feature we build is evaluated against whether a user can understand, control, and leave it. On this page 01 / Identity 02 / Moderation 03 / Verification 04 / Privacy 05 / Account control 01 / Identity Who you are, who you appear to be, and who can tell the difference. PARA is designed around personas and proof bundles, not a single public name. You can operate with different masks for different communities, and you can choose how much of your verification stack is visible in each context. Pseudonymity and personas View persona features Multiple personas per account, switchable without logout. Each persona can have its own display name, bio, and political placement. Personas are not burner accounts; they are first-class identity surfaces. Proof bundles View verification layers INE scan for Mexican voter verification. Biometric gate and app-state auto-lock. QR export to share verified bundles offline. Custom surface builder to control what each context sees. 02 / Moderation Rules, tools, and proportionality. We enforce baseline rules through human review and automated signals. We also design for composable safety—labelers, user controls, and community-specific norms—so moderation is not a single gatekeeper. Baseline Community Guidelines Safety first, respect others, be authentic, follow the rules. These four principles govern what we remove or limit on PARA services we operate. Composable Labelers and user controls Where the protocol supports it, users can subscribe to additional labelers and adjust safety settings. Communities can add context on top of baseline rules. Appeals. If we restrict or suspend your account, you may appeal within fourteen (14) days. Late or bare appeals may be declined. We retain discretion to make final calls. 03 / Verification Trust without forced exposure. Validation matters for civic participation, but not every user should have to expose their real name to participate. PARA holds both at once. What verification enables View benefits Access to verified-only communities and representative channels. Higher weight in certain aggregation or ranking surfaces. Reputation that persists across personas where you choose to link it. What anonymity protects View protections Freedom of thought for people in unsafe political environments. Whistleblowing and dissent without personal exposure. Exploration of political identity before committing to a public position. 04 / Privacy Data visibility in a federated system. PARA is built on open protocol infrastructure. That means public posts may be replicated by third-party services outside our direct control. We design the product to make visibility legible, not hidden. Public by default Posts, votes, and profile fields are public unless the product offers a restricted mode. Federation means copies may exist elsewhere. Messages Direct and group messaging uses end-to-end encryption where the protocol supports it. Metadata may still be visible to infrastructure operators. Retention We keep data as long as needed to operate the service and meet legal obligations. Deletion requests go to support and are handled when verifiable. 05 / Account control You should be able to leave, export, or appeal. Account deletion, data export, and appeals are not afterthoughts. They are part of the trust surface. Deletion You can delete your account where the product provides the feature. We remove content from services we control, subject to backups, legal holds, and safety needs. Export Repository exports are possible through protocol-native tools. Contact support if you need help locating the right export path. Read next Trust and safety should connect product, thesis, and protocol.
